sections.h2: What are my choices when I want to sell a house in Perry?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell the house yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes it as it stands. The right route depends on the condition of the house, how quickly you need the money, and how much work you are willing to do before strangers walk through it.

Perry draws buyers from the Robins Air Force Base workforce and from travelers on Interstate 75, so a tidy house in a good location can find a taker on the open market. A house with a failing roof, an unfinished permit, a probate cloud or a tenant who will not leave usually sits longer. That is the situation where owners in Perry look at a direct cash sale.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure and often the highest price, paired with showings, repair requests after inspection and a timeline set by the buyer's lender.
  • Sale by owner: you keep the agent fee for yourself but handle pricing, paperwork, negotiation and the buyer's questions about the house.
  • Cash sale: a faster, simpler closing with no repairs on your side, usually at a lower price than a fully prepared listing would bring.

Compare written numbers for each route. A higher list price can shrink once agent fees, repairs and carrying costs through a longer wait are subtracted.

sections.h2: What makes Perry, Georgia, different from the rest of Houston County?
sections.html:
Perry is the oldest town in Houston County and was the first municipality in the county. The city's own history page says it was incorporated in 1824 and named for Oliver Hazard Perry, the naval hero of the War of 1812. When Houston County was formed in 1821, a small settlement called Wattsville was picked as county seat, and that settlement became Perry.

The original city limits formed a rough circle with a half-mile radius from the courthouse square, with Big Indian Creek marking part of the edge. Downtown took its present shape in the 1910s and 1920s along Carroll Street. Houses close to the square are among the oldest in town, so expect a buyer or inspector to look closely at roofs, wiring and plumbing from that era.

Growth took off after June 1941, when the War Department approved an air depot near Wellston that later became Robins Air Force Base. The city says the base employed between 15,000 and 25,000 people and that Perry's population quadrupled between 1940 and 1960. Interstate 75 came through in the 1960s. In 1990 the Georgia National Fairgrounds and Agricenter opened at a cost of $26.2 million, and the city reports more than 260 events a year there, including the Georgia National Fair each October with more than half a million visitors.

Perry Parkway, on the east side, was built out through the 1990s and early 2000s. The city's history notes that it pulled some activity away from downtown and spurred development on the outskirts. Sellers on the east side and sellers near the square are therefore dealing with homes of quite different ages.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Perry homes and owners?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts puts Perry at 25,699 residents in its July 1, 2025 estimate, up from 20,624 counted in April 2020 and 13,839 in 2010. The table below lists the housing and household figures that matter most to a seller.

sections.h2: Which City of Perry rules can affect a sale?
sections.html:
The city's Community Development department handles permits, inspections, planning and code compliance. Permit applications go through an online portal, attachments must be PDF files, and a state licensed contractor who has never pulled a Perry permit is asked to call the department first.

  • Administrative decisions: staff approve sign permits, building permits, site plans, final plats, minor subdivisions and zoning compliance, plus a certificate of appropriateness for work in historic districts.
  • Planning Commission items: variances, administrative appeals, preliminary plats, special exceptions, rezonings and map or text amendments go to the Planning Commission with a staff report.
  • Code Compliance: this bureau responds to complaints about derelict vehicles, illegal signs, overgrown grass, and trash or debris, under the city's Chapter 19 on nuisances.

If your house has an open code complaint or a permit that was never closed, ask Community Development for the status before you set a price. A cash buyer can take over those loose ends, though the price will reflect them.

sections.h2: How do Houston County property taxes affect a Perry sale?
sections.html:
Perry sits inside Houston County, so the county Tax Assessor sets value and the Tax Commissioner collects the bill. Both keep an office in the courthouse at 201 Perry Parkway, and the Tax Commissioner lists weekday hours from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The county explains that Georgia values property as of January 1 each year and taxes it at 40% of fair market value, with one mill equal to $1.00 for each $1,000 of assessed value. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the current bill on your parcel and for any amount still unpaid, since the closing agent will need both.

  • Homestead exemption: the first application is due at the Tax Assessor's Office by April 1 of the year it is first claimed, and it renews on its own until the owner changes or asks for a different exemption.
  • Appeal window: after the Board of Tax Assessors changes a value, the owner has 45 days from receiving the notice to appeal.
  • Appeal path: the Board of Assessors reviews first, then the county Board of Equalization, with arbitration offered in its place and Superior Court as the last step.

The county states that an appeal can challenge taxability, value or uniformity, and cannot rest on a complaint about the amount of tax. When ownership changes, the automatic renewal of the exemption ends, so your buyer files their own application.

sections.h2: What happens at closing and recording in Perry?
sections.html:
A deed cannot be recorded with the clerk of superior court until the real estate transfer tax has been paid. The Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority describes that tax as an excise tax on the sale, separate from property tax, and reports it on Form PT-61, which is filled out online and printed to go in with the deed.

Only one PT-61 goes with each deed. For a Perry house, the deed is filed with the Houston County clerk of superior court. Ask your closing attorney or title company who pays the transfer tax in your contract and what the rate is for your deed, because the answer depends on the sale terms.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Perry house?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when time and certainty matter more than the last few thousand dollars of price. These are the situations Perry owners bring up most:

  • An inherited house that nobody plans to live in and that needs cleaning out.
  • A house with deferred repairs that would cost more than the owner wants to put in before listing.
  • A mortgage that has fallen behind and a deadline from the lender.
  • A rental with tenants or turnover problems that the owner is tired of managing.
  • A code complaint or lapsed permit that would slow a financed buyer's inspection.

Ask any buyer for the offer in writing, the closing date, and a clear statement of who pays each closing cost. Then compare it with what a listing would net after fees and repairs.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Perry house as is?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell a Perry house in any condition. A cash buyer takes it as it stands, and a listing buyer may ask for repairs after the inspection. Decide in advance which repairs you would agree to, and which you would turn down.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about a property value in Perry?
faqs.a: Contact the Houston County Tax Assessor, whose office is inside the courthouse at 201 Perry Parkway. The county lists (478) 218-4750 for the front desk. Property tax bills come from the Tax Commissioner, who has a Perry office at the same address.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a new assessment on a Perry house?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from receiving the notice of change. File the appeal in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors. If the board leaves the value as it is, the case moves to the county Board of Equalization, and arbitration is available instead.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption carry over to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Houston County renews an exemption automatically only for the same owner, and a change of ownership ends that. The buyer applies for their own exemption by April 1 of the first year they want it.

faqs.q: What paperwork records the sale of a Perry house?
faqs.a: The deed and a Form PT-61 transfer tax filing go to the Houston County clerk of superior court. The PT-61 is completed online through the Georgia clerks' authority. Your closing attorney or title company usually handles both.
